users_and_stakeholders.interest: Their bike ready by 17:30 when promised.

steps: The manager reads the drop-off tags.
The manager decides what can be done today.
The manager tells each mechanic their jobs.
problems: Three or four commuters a week find their bike not ready at 17:30.
Bolts get tightened by feel, not to the maker's torque.
cites: [A:A01 "three or four commuters a week find their bike not ready at 17:30"]
[A:A01 "Out: bike sales, hire bikes, the Saturday maintenance class."]

inputs.description: Typed drop-off forms, about 20 each morning.
inputs.format: plain text, one form per ticket
constraints: The customer's description of the fault
cites: [S:S01 §whole file]

glossary.meaning: The standard time a job takes, from the bench-time table.
cites: [A:A01 "Bench minutes: the standard time a job takes, from the bench-time table."]

glossary.meaning: How tight a bolt is, in newton metres.
A bike promised back by 17:30 the day it was dropped off.

acceptance_tests.words: I give it a fortnight of made-up tags, and every bike promised for 17:30 fits in the day's bench time.

ranks.what: Reference documents in the context pack
Official documentation on the maker's own site

confidence.high: The row quotes the form and the bench-time table line that decided it.
confidence.medium: A reputable secondary source; not expected here.
confidence.low: Inferred or one weak source; such a row is marked 'ask the workshop' and raised as a question.

conflicts: The higher rank wins within its own area.
A conflict the ranks do not settle is reported with both citations, never decided silently.

output.description: A repair queue, one row per drop-off form, in working order. A tag with no fault description is refused as 'ask at the counter'.
output.format: Table, one row per ticket, in queue order
